record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Show that spacetime metrics that are smoothly or distributionally extendible across Cauchy horizons form a measure-zero subset of all spacetimes, in an appropriate sense.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the class of smooth (3+1)-dimensional globally hyperbolic spacetimes (M, g) arising as maximal globally hyperbolic developments of smooth initial data (Σ, h, K) for the vacuum Einstein equations Ric(g) = 0 (or, more generally, for a reasonable Einstein–matter system). Some such developments possess a Cauchy horizon across which the metric g admits a nontrivial extension as a Lorentzian metric — either smoothly (C^∞) or in a distributional sense (e.g. as a C^0 Lorentzian metric with locally square-integrable Christoffel symbols, so that the Einstein equations make sense weakly).

Equip the space of admissible initial data sets (Σ, h, K) with a suitable topology and a notion of "generic" or "measure-zero" subset (for instance, a Baire-generic, prevalent, or measure-theoretic notion on an appropriate infinite-dimensional space of initial data).

Prove that the set of initial data whose maximal globally hyperbolic development admits a smooth, or even a distributional, Lorentzian extension across a Cauchy horizon forms a measure-zero (negligible / non-generic) subset of all admissible initial data, in an appropriate precise sense to be formulated.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a precise formulation of the Strong Cosmic Censorship conjecture (in its C^∞ and H^1_loc forms). It remains open in general. Substantial progress has been made: linear and nonlinear results show generic curvature blow-up and C^2 inextendibility for perturbations of Kerr/Schwarzschild interiors, and recent work establishes Lipschitz/H^1 inextendibility in various settings, but a full proof of genericity of inextendibility for the Einstein equations is not available as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: The Strong Cosmic Censorship Conjecture (Van de Moortel, 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: For generic initial data for the vacuum equations or suitable Einstein–matter systems, the maximal Cauchy development is inextendible. Several formulations (C^0, H^1) remain open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The strong cosmic censorship conjecture, of which generic inextendibility at Cauchy horizons is the central content, is still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Lipschitz inextendibility of weak null singularities (Invent. Math. 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Generically curvature blows up at the Cauchy horizon, turning it into a weak null singularity.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress toward genericity of inextendibility has been obtained, but the full conjecture is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Strong cosmic censorship — M. Dafermos
status_evidence.snippet: Cauchy horizons are the sole threat to determinism; conjecturally they are unstable for generic data.
status_evidence.claim: The genericity/measure-zero formulation of inextendibility at Cauchy horizons is an active open problem.
